title: One-to-one and many-to-many
summary: A user and their profile; books and tags with skip navigations; and a join entity when the link has data of its own.

steps.title: One-to-one
body: Each user has at most one profile, and each profile belongs to one user:
public Profile? Profile { get; set; }          // optional: a user may not have one yet
public int UserId { get; set; }                // the foreign key lives here
public User User { get; set; } = null!;

With a reference navigation on both sides, EF Core cannot tell which one is the dependent **unless** one side has the foreign key property. `Profile.UserId` settles it: `Profile` is the dependent. EF Core also gives `UserId` a **unique** index, because two profiles must not point at the same user.
Fluent API spelling: `model.Entity<User>().HasOne(u => u.Profile).WithOne(p => p.User).HasForeignKey<Profile>(p => p.UserId);`

code: public User User { get; set; } = null!;
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=app.db");
steps.explain: Only the dependent table (`Profiles`) gets a foreign key column, and it is uniquely indexed: one profile per user. `Users` has no `ProfileId` column at all; `User.Profile` is found by looking up `Profiles.UserId`.

steps.title: Many-to-many
body: A book has many tags; a tag is on many books. Neither table can hold the other's key: a third **join table** holds pairs. Give both sides a collection, and EF Core creates the join table for you:

The join table is `BookTag` with columns `BooksId` and `TagsId`, a composite primary key over both. You never see it in C#: `book.Tags.Add(scifi)` inserts a `BookTag` row on save. These collections are called **skip navigations**, because they skip over the join table.

code: protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=library.db");
steps.explain: Two books carry `classic`. The hidden join table holds one row per link: Dune with sci-fi, Dune with classic, Emma with classic. (`Set<Dictionary<string, object>>("BookTag")` is how you reach the join entity EF Core made for you; you will rarely need it.)

steps.title: When the link has data: a join entity
body: A member borrows many books, and a book is borrowed by many members. But a loan also has **data of its own**: when it was borrowed, when it is due. Skip navigations have nowhere to put that. Make the join an entity:
public Member Member { get; set; } = null!;
public Book Book { get; set; } = null!;

That is simply two one-to-many relationships: a member has many loans, a book has many loans. Use skip navigations for a plain link, and an explicit join entity the moment the link needs a date, a quantity, a role, or a history (the same book borrowed twice by one member).

steps.prompt: Skip navigations, or an explicit join entity?
items: Students and the clubs they belong to
Orders and products, with a quantity per product
Actors and films, with the role each actor played
Members and books they borrowed, with due dates
steps.explain: If you can describe the link with only the two ids, skip navigations do. As soon as there is something to say *about* the link, it is an entity.

steps.prompt: What primary key does EF Core give the `BookTag` join table it creates?
options: None: join tables have no key
steps.explain: The pair is the identity of a link, and the composite key also stops the same tag being attached to the same book twice.

steps.title: Students and courses
prompt: Model students and courses with **skip navigations**:

Then write `void Enrol(SchoolDb db, int studentId, int courseId)` (at the top) that links an existing student to an existing course and saves. Enrolling twice must not fail: do nothing if the student is already in the course.
starter: void Enrol(SchoolDb db, int studentId, int courseId)
solution: void Enrol(SchoolDb db, int studentId, int courseId)
var student = db.Students.Include(s => s.Courses).Single(s => s.Id == studentId);
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=school.db");
template: dojoDb.Students.AddRange(new Student { Name = "Ana" }, new Student { Name = "Ben" });
dojoDb.Courses.AddRange(new Course { Title = "Maths" }, new Course { Title = "Art" });
using (var dojoDb = new SchoolDb()) { Enrol(dojoDb, 1, 1); Enrol(dojoDb, 1, 2); Enrol(dojoDb, 2, 1); }
Dojo.Eq("Ana takes Maths and Art", new List<string> { "Art", "Maths" }, dojoDb.Students.Where(s => s.Id == 1).SelectMany(s => s.Courses).Select(c => c.Title).OrderBy(t => t).ToList());
Dojo.Eq("Maths has two students", 2, dojoDb.Courses.Where(c => c.Title == "Maths").Select(c => c.Students.Count).Single());
Dojo.Eq("enrolling twice adds no extra link", 3, dojoDb.Set<Dictionary<string, object>>("CourseStudent").Count());
hints: Load the student **with** their courses (`Include(s => s.Courses)`), so you can check whether the course is already there.
